Latin word

eōrum

eōrum, eārum

pronoun: genitive plural of is (eōrum masculine and neuter, eārum feminine)

their (someone else’s)

In this lexicon

  • their

    the recommended word · classical · Liv. 5.47.4: clangōre eōrum ālārumque crepitū; Varr. RR 2.1.7: vōx eārum

Examples

  • namque clangōre eōrum ālārumque crepitū excitus M. Mānlius

    for Marcus Manlius, woken by their honking and the flapping of their wingsLiv. 5.47.4

    In the entry for their

  • vōx eārum nōn mē, sed bē sonāre vidētur

    Their voice seems to sound not “meh” but “beh”.Varr. RR 2.1.7

    In the entry for their

  • nē, quās ibi posuerīs ad partum, nōn līberōs eārum, sed ipsās quaerās

    so that you aren’t looking for the snails you put there to breed, rather than their youngVarr. RR 3.14.1
